Name: KaDFIR_FaultInfo[CiDFIR_DTC_NotSupported]
Comment:
Mapa:
Calibration Note:
A composite of two arrays each which spans from 1 to CcDFIR_NoOf_DTCs. This calibration array is not made available to other rings directly. It is actually the composite of KaDFIR_FaultType and KaDFIR_LightEnable which are made available to other rings as output from DFIR. For each diagnostic there exists a single calibration byte which defines both calibration arrays above. This calibration array is ONLY defined in the data dictionary for purposes of providing software traceability. Other rings must access this information via the KaDFIR_FaultType and KaDFIR_LightEnable calibrations.

Mapa:
Calibration Note:
A composite of two arrays each which spans from 1 to CcDFIR_NoOf_DTCs. This calibration array is not made available to other rings directly. It is actually the composite of KaDFIR_FaultType and KaDFIR_LightEnable which are made available to other rings as output from DFIR. For each diagnostic there exists a single calibration byte which defines both calibration arrays above. This calibration array is ONLY defined in the data dictionary for purposes of providing software traceability. Other rings must access this information via the KaDFIR_FaultType and KaDFIR_LightEnable calibrations.

Name: KeDDCC_b_ExitImmedRateExpEnbl
Comment:
Mapa:
Calibration Note:
Enable Exponential TorqReqExit by using the Immediate Reserve Rate Exit method. When CbTRUE, VeDDCC_M_ImmdtReserve is initialized as VeETQR_M_EngTorqueUnmanaged VeDDCC_M_EngReqImmed when DDCR mode changes from activated to disabled.At each step VeDDCC_M_ImmdtReserve = VeDDCC_M_ImmdtReserve(prev) - VeDDCC_M_ImmdtReserve (prev)*VeDDCC_M_TorqReqExitImmedRate. VeDDCC_M_EngReqImmed = VeETQR_M_EngTorqUnmanaged - VeDDCC_M_ImmdtReserve. When CbFALSE, VeDDCC_M_EngReqImmed = VeDDCC_M_EngReqImmed(prev) +VeDDCC_M_TorqReqExitImmedRate. For AT with DDCR calibration already completed in previous sw level, set this value to CbFALSE. For new AT calibration or for MT calibration set this to CbTRUE.

Name: KeDDCC_b_ExitImmedRateExpEnbl
Comment:
Mapa:
Calibration Note:

When CbTRUE, VeDDCC_M_ImmdtReserve is initialized as VeETQR_M_EngTorqueUnmanaged VeDDCC_M_EngReqImmed when DDCR mode changes from activated to disabled.At each step VeDDCC_M_ImmdtReserve = VeDDCC_M_ImmdtReserve(prev) - VeDDCC_M_ImmdtReserve (prev)*VeDDCC_M_TorqReqExitImmedRate. VeDDCC_M_EngReqImmed = VeETQR_M_EngTorqUnmanaged - VeDDCC_M_ImmdtReserve. When CbFALSE, VeDDCC_M_EngReqImmed = VeDDCC_M_EngReqImmed(prev) +VeDDCC_M_TorqReqExitImmedRate. For AT with DDCR calibration already completed in previous sw level, set this value to CbFALSE. For new AT calibration or for MT calibration set this to CbTRUE.

Name: KeECTI_T_BHReboundDeltaMax
Comment:
Mapa:
Calibration Note:
This cal is for the control block heater detection only. It does not affect any of the ECT sensor diagnostics. After a block heater is used, and then engine is subsequently started, coolant temperature will generally drop temporarely and then startrising again. The control block heater algorithm looks for this dip in the coolant temperature and then looks for the start of rise again. When the risinf of the sensor indicated coolant temperature happens, the blending of the sudo coolant temperature towards the sensor indicated coolant temperature will start. This cal represents how much does the sensor indicated coolant temperature has to rise again after dropping before the blending would start. This cal should be set to abput two degrees,not too much higher to identify the start of the rise quickly, and not too much lower to avoid misidentification of the start of the rise due to noise in the coolant temperature signal.

Comment:

Calibration Note:
Minimum time between successful learn sequences. The learn sequence may run continuously while the engine is in sync and phasers are parked (and no faults exist). However, there isnt any delay if a learn sequence is disabled or aborted prior to completing. For example, if a learn sequence encounters too many invalid cam edges (out-of-rangevalues), then the learn is disabled and a new learn is re-started as soon as conditions allow (without any delay).

When set True (in conjunction with KeEPSC_e_CrkSensorType = CeEPSR_e_Bidirectional), the HWIO software shall perform Reverse Crank Processing during the appropriate Autostop/Autostart sequence. This also means a fast Autostart may be allowed upon the subsequent Autostart (assuming all other necessary criteria for fast Autostart is satisfied within other areas of software such as fuel, spark, etc.). Note: fast Autostarts are limited to 12vSS Applications.

Comment:
Mapa:
Calibration Note:

A slow (i.e. larger value) time constant is needed to keep the engine speed above the turbine speed. If this cal is too low, thenengine might cross turbine speed. Default is 0.1. Cal out is 0.

Name: KeSPDC_K_KeepEngAbvTbRefCurrExp

Name: KeSPDC_K_RefDsrd4RefCurrDltDcy
Comment:
Mapa:
Calibration Note:
Decay factor used on VeSPDR_n_RefDsrd4RefCurrDelta to reduce it to zero. This is only applied after closed throttle downshifts where the engine speed was above turbine speed (i.e. VeSPDR_b_DwnShftKeepEngAbovTrbn goes from CbTRUE to CbFALSE). Once the shift is complete, then the delta will be multiplied by this factor every 12.5 ms loop. The lower this calibration is, the faster VeSPDR_n_RefDsrd4RefCurr will become equal to VeSPDR_n_RefDsrd. To make the decay slower, use a higher value like 0.9.

Name: KeSPDC_Pct_PedalStlSaverEnter
Comment:
Mapa:
Calibration Note:
This is the effective accelerator pedal position threshold to enter stall saver. VeDTRR_Pct_AccelEffPosition must be less than or equal to KeSPDC_PctPedalStlSaverEnter to activate Stall Saver. This calibration must be lower than KeSPDC_Pct_PedalStlSaverExit. One other condition to enter stall saver is that the actual current engine rpm to see if it is equal to or lower than the minimum of KeSPDC_n_StallSaver and (VeSPDC_n_RefDsrd - KeSPDC_n_StallSaverEnterOfst).

Name: KeSPDC_b_EngAbovTrbnExitIfCross
Comment:
Mapa:
Calibration Note:
If CbTRUE, then VeSPDR_b_DwnShftKeepEngAbovTrbn will reset to CbFALSE if the engine speed falls below turbine speed during a closed throttle downshift. If CbFALSE, then VeSPDR_b_DwnShftKeepEngAbovTrbn will retain its value until the shift is completed. If your application keeps engine above turbine for your normal coastdown, then you should cal this to CbFALSE. If your application keeps engine below turbine, then you should calibrate this to CbTRUE. Default and cal out value is CbTRUE.

Name: KtDTRC_M_DeltaNeutral
Comment:
Mapa:
Calibration Note:
This table is used to ramp from the new launch torque to the neutral progression torque after launch active pedal becomes CbFALSE. Inputs are the latched delta difference between these two torques at the falling edge of launch active pedal and the time since the falling edge. If the delta difference between launch torque and neutral torque is very high, then the likely cause is from overscaled values between launch and normal neutral or pedal progression tables. These large overscaled values can change very quickly and its important to ramp out the delta torque quickly to prevent an (overscaled) drop in either the neutral or pedal torque causing the blended torque to drop suddenly and ramp slowly. If the delta difference between launch torque and neutral torque is fairly small, then it is important to ramp slowly until the vehicle speed blending is finished so that there is minimal change in the overall launch torque (fast ramping in this scenario could make the launch torque drop toofast causing the launch to feel slugish). Cal out values are all 100. Default values are: [[0.1, 5, 100][0.5, 5, 100][5, 50, 100][10, 100, 100][512, 512, 512]]

Oœ X:
Calibration Note:
This calibratable axis uses VeDTRC_t_LnchActPedFallEdge to determine which column of KtDTRC_M_DeltaNeutral should be used to ramp out delta launch torque after launch active pedal becomes CbFALSE. The values of this table represent the time since launch active pedal became CbFALSE. Default values are [0.1, 0.35, 1].

Oœ Y:
Calibration Note:
This calibratable axis uses VeDTRC_DeltaM_NeutralFallEdge to determine which row of KtDTRC_M_DeltaNeutral should be used to ramp out delta launch torque after launch active pedal becomes CbFALSE. The values of this table are signed and represent thelatched value of the difference between launch torque and the normal neutral progression torque (VeDTRC_M_Neutral_wLaunchMod) at the falling edge of launch active pedal becoming CbFALSE. Negative values correspond to launch torques that are higher than VeDTRC_M_Neutral_wLaunchMod. Positive values correspond to launch torques that are lower than VeDTRC_M_Neutral_wLaunchMod. Default values are [-50, -25, 0, 25, 50].
AxisX.Name: KnDTRC_t_LnchActPedFallAxis
AxisY.Name: KnDTRC_M_DeltaNeutralAxis

First column of table is used for Coastdown mode. Second column is used when in Idle or OpenLoop. First row is used when torque VeSPDR_M_ImmedReq is increasing at the end of the shift. For Chassis controllersCiVLTI_i_UserGainSwRefVoltCkt and CiVLTI_i_ManApplySwRefVoltCktcan be selected to report C0880 and C0890 respectively. Hereorder of selection may or may not be important.
